metadata.case_name: LEUNG YUK-KWAN v. MAPLE PROFESSIONAL BEAUTY CENTRE LTD.

plaintiff.occupation_before: First year student in the Higher Diploma in Travel and Tourism; private tutor
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: Air hostess / work in the tourist industry

injuries.description: Scald injury to right leg causing blistering, ulceration and permanent scarring of the right lower extremity
injuries.body_part: right leg / right shin / right lower extremity
source: a so-called "fat-losing" electric blanket to her person, operating it in such a negligent fashion that the plaintiff's right leg was severely scalded, causing immediate pain and eventually blistering and ulceration.

When the plaintiff was assessed by Dr Chung Ho-yin of Queen Mary Hospital on 28 October 2000, a patch of main wound at the middle part of the right shin with yellowish centre and granulation tissue at the periphery and satellite lesions of healed wounds at the lateral side of the main wound were readily observed.

This lady suffers ugly scar over the front and back of her right lower extremity. The scar over the front of the right leg is very ugly. It may be improved over time (as long as four years). They are the direct result of a scald injury caused by either the malfunction of a beauty machine or lack of proper management of such machine.
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of knee or lower leg

injuries.description: Psychiatric injury: adjustment disorder and depressive reaction to her injuries with psychiatric disability assessed at 15% whole person impairment
source: "I think Ms Leung suffers from adjustment disorder to the wound she sustained. She places undue emphasis on her physical appearance. She also harbours catastrophic, irrational and rigid thoughts in relation to her injury and its effects on her life."

On 14 August 2001, a psychiatric assessment was conducted by Dr Peter Ho Pang-yin. Dr Ho opined that the plaintiff was suffering from depressive reaction to her injuries. The symptoms presented included reduced zest, interest, drive, motivation, appetite, sleep disturbance, fatigue, feeling of worthlessness and of suicidal ideas, impaired concentration and memory, and associated somatically induced constipation. He assessed whole person impairment at 15 per cent from the psychiatric disability.

manifestations.description: Blistering and ulceration of the right leg wounds
Unsightly/ugly scarring (pigmented scars, large round pigmented scar 45 x 50 mm, long vertical linear scar 120 mm, other small pigmented dots)
Toes appear to be slightly distorted
Preoccupation with the wound and desire for total removal of the scar; lack of insight and resistance to psychotherapy
Depressive reaction with reduced zest, interest, drive, motivation; appetite and sleep disturbance; fatigue; feelings of worthlessness; suicidal ideas

treatments_future: psychiatric counselling (provision made for one year)

losses.description: Unsightly permanent scarring of the right lower extremity (pigmented and linear scars) resulting from the scald injury.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Lost considerable confidence and self-esteem as a consequence of the accident.
The plaintiff's dream of becoming an air stewardess or a model, or working in the tourist industry, has been shattered.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: The accident resulted in her dropping out from the Higher Diploma in Travel and Tourism course; she would have graduated in June 2002 but was unable to complete her studies due to psychological and psychiatric disturbances.
